title: Renting out a bank account — social media recruitment (demo script)
summary: Synthetic training case. A retail customer says on social media that their account is for rent, and calls it safe and legal. The account first receives a small test credit. The trainee decides whether to interview the customer, draft a suspicious transaction report, hold outbound payments or exit. Exiting without a report is an incomplete path. It is inspired by a public police enforcement briefing on renting and selling accounts. It is not a real customer file.

teaching.disclaimer: Synthetic training scenario inspired by public enforcement reporting. Not official case files; no real customer data.

sources.label: Police press, April 2025 operation on account rental (URL not in the course brief)

rules.when: The customer admits the account is used by a third party, or admits renting out or selling control of the account
rules.note: Normal use must not continue. Once a test credit has arrived, exiting without a report does not meet the rule.

rules.when: An unknown third party controls the account, and third-party credits have already arrived
rules.note: It must not be treated as helping a friend or as customer service. Rules come before any model score.

nodes.title: Social media recruitment alert
nodes.prompt: Synthetic Customer B posts that their bank account is for rent, with the words "safe and legal". The account has just received a small test credit. The payer is not the customer.

nodes.title: How to start on the alert
nodes.prompt: The post and the test credit are both on file. Do you interview the customer, report and exit now, or close the post as a joke?

choices.label: Interview the customer
choices.rationale: Get the facts on account control first, then let R1 decide.

choices.label: Draft an STR and exit
choices.rationale: The post plus the test credit is enough to report. There is no need to wait for the customer to admit it.

choices.label: Close as a social media joke
choices.rationale: Poor teaching start. The test credit is still there, and later credits will trigger R2.

nodes.title: Customer admits renting out the account
nodes.prompt: The customer says a company pays them rent, and their only job is to hand over verification codes. The other side said this is normal. The customer does not control the account. Rule R1: once renting is admitted, normal use must not continue.

nodes.title: After the rental admission
nodes.prompt: R1 is met, and the test credit is still there. Do you report and exit, exit without reporting, or add monitoring and let use continue?

choices.label: Draft an STR and exit
choices.rationale: Meets R1. The account control facts and the test credit are kept on record together.

choices.label: Exit only, no report
choices.rationale: Incomplete teaching path. Exiting does not erase the test credit that already happened.

choices.label: Add monitoring and allow continued use
choices.rationale: Overrides R1. The override is an event. It does not delete the rental facts.

nodes.title: Credits after the test
nodes.prompt: After the test credit, several third-party credits arrive, with requests to move the money on quickly. Rule R2: when an unknown third party controls the account and credits have arrived, it must not be treated as helping a friend.

nodes.title: Action after the credits
nodes.prompt: R2 is met. Do you hold outbound payments and draft a report, exit and report, or close it as helping a friend?

choices.label: Hold outbound payments and draft an STR
choices.rationale: The stop-payment-and-report exit that meets R2.

choices.label: Close as helping a friend
choices.rationale: Poor teaching path. The rule already says the case must not be closed this way.

nodes.title: Suspicious transaction report drafted
nodes.prompt: Reporting exit. The rental facts or the post flag stay in the state. The exit did not clear them.

nodes.title: Exit without a report
nodes.prompt: Poor teaching path. The relationship has ended, but the test credit and the rental admission did not go into a suspicious transaction report.

nodes.title: Outbound payments held and report drafted
nodes.prompt: Outbound payments are on hold, and the report has been drafted. If R1 was overridden earlier, the override flag is still there.

nodes.title: Closed as helping a friend
nodes.prompt: Poor teaching path. R2 was ignored. The dashboard should later mark this session as not following the rules.
